newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka warns troops of cyanide on stamps.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka warns troops of cyanide on stamps.

text.p: Sri Lanka's army has warned soldiers deployed in the north not to buy postage stamps from local outlets as some of them were found coated with cyanide, the Weekend Express newspaper said on Saturday.
Traces of cyanide had been found in the gum on some of the stamps, the paper said.
Soldiers deployed against Tamil Tiger rebels were also advised not to accept food from the public to prevent guerrilla attempts to poison them, the paper said.
A military spokesman said he had no immediate information about the report, but added that it was possible the rebels could try to poison troops.
Government forces took control of much of the northern Jaffna peninsula earlier this year after a series of offensives against Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels.
But rebel infiltrators mingling with the public continue to stage hit-and-run attacks on government troops.
Two soldiers were killed and one was wounded on Saturday morning when rebels detonated a claymore mine in Point Pedro, in the northeast of the peninsula, the spokesman said.

The Tigers, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the mainly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island's north and east, carry cyanide suicide capsules to be taken in the event of being captured.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic conflict now in its 14th year.
